text:
Sam - AE: Hey team — Customer X is asking for a Private deployment POC. They specifically want: BYOK via their HSM, ephemeral certs for the control plane handshake, and a short checklist for the network/KMS handoff. Also flagged price difference question: does Dedicated vs Private change the POC pricing?
Emma (SE): Quick answers first: Dedicated = Redwood-managed HW in our infra (reserved capacity) vs Private = customer VPC / on-prem with our private control plane. Pricing for a POC can be adjusted but Private has extra engineering/setup time.
Raj (Solutions): Agree with Emma. For BYOK w/ HSM we usually do either: 1) an HSM bridge where customer keeps keys and we talk to it over a pinned tunnel, or 2) a customer-managed KMS with signed certs we trust. Both have different support SOWs.
Sam - AE: Customer prefers option 1 (HSM bridge). They asked about cert exchange mechanism and whether we can accept a PKCS#11 endpoint.
Emma (SE): We don't talk PKCS#11 directly from hosted control plane. For Private we can deploy a connector that does PKCS#11 -> TLS to our control plane. Typical handoff: customer provides a CA cert + an intermediate they sign a CSR with. We return a server cert (PEM) and an OCSP URL if needed.
Emma (SE): Minimal checklist I can drop here: 
- Network: VPC peering or private relay + allowed CIDRs for control plane
- Auth: Service certs (client+server) and optional mTLS for admin routes
- KMS: PKCS#11 endpoint OR external KMS REST endpoint + usage ACLs
- Secrets flow: ephemeral tokens (1h default) + option for long-lived service identity certs
- Logs: syslog endpoint or S3 export for audit logs
- Test plan: smoke generation, KV cache warmup, failover test

Raj (Solutions): Adding to that — if they want offline HSM (air-gapped), we need a runbook for manual key wrapping during deployment. That adds ~3 days to setup.
Sam - AE: Noted. Can you draft the exact CSR template and the TLS ciphers we accept? They asked for the commands.
Emma (SE): Paste below — this is what we give customers for server cert CSR (example):
```
openssl req -new -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -keyout customer_private.key -out customer.csr -subj '/CN=customerx-controlplane/O=CustomerX' -reqexts req_ext -config <(cat /etc/ssl/openssl.cnf 
[req_ext]
subjectAltName = DNS:control.private.customerx.internal,IP:10.0.0.5)
```
We accept ECDSA P-256 or RSA-4096. For TLS ciphers we prefer modern profiles: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384. No CBC.
Sam - AE: Great. For the HSM keywrap flow — do we do a wrapped key exchange or ephemeral signing only?
Emma (SE): For POC we recommend ephemeral signing + wrapped key for data keys. Flow: customer generates a DEK inside HSM, wraps with our public wrapping key, we import the wrapped DEK into the runtime. We provide the public wrapping key as a signed cert. That avoids exposing unwrapped keys.
Maria (PM): Any compliance blockers we should flag to legal? Customer noted they need SOC2 + customer-managed KMS key attestations.
Raj (Solutions): We'll need an Attestation doc + key rotation policy. For POC we can provide a limited attestation (non-audited) and follow up with full artifacts if they move to private prod.
Sam - AE: Who owns the secure transfer of certs? SFTP? Signed email?
Emma (SE): We prefer a short-lived S3 presigned URL or SFTP with MFA. For automation, customers upload their signed CSR to our presigned S3, we post our cert back to the same bucket with a one-hour expiry. If they can't use S3, SFTP is fine.
Sam - AE: Customer asked whether Hosted API keys could be used instead of full Private for quick dev tests.
Raj (Solutions): Hosted API keys are easiest for feature validation but won't satisfy their data residency / BYOK requirements. Use Hosted for demo traffic, Private for anything that needs their HSM or VPC isolation.
infra-bot: Deployment checklist created: POC-1234 — Private POC onboarding (assigned: Emma).
Emma (SE): I'll put the CSR template, presigned S3 instructions, and the HSM keywrap guide into a single zip and upload to the JIRA ticket. Also will include expected timeline: 3 business days for connector + 1 day for cert exchange + 1 day for smoke tests (total ~5 business days).
Sam - AE: Can we give a ballpark POC price to the customer now? They asked for a figure to justify budget.
Raj (Solutions): Ballpark: $XXk for Private POC (covers engineering time + infra). If they accept Dedicated POC (our reserved pool) it's typically 30% less since less networking work. I'll draft a short one-pager with numbers.
Maria (PM): I'll loop Legal for the attestation note. Sam, can you confirm the customer can meet the network pre-reqs (open ports, egress to our control plane IPs)?
Sam - AE: I'll confirm and share their network diagram.
Emma (SE): One more operational note: set cert TTL to 24 hours for POC by default, rotate daily. We can shorten to 1h if they want stricter ephemeral creds.
Sam - AE: Thanks all. I'll update the customer with the CSR, the S3 option, timeline, and the draft price. Ping me if anything changes. :thumbsup:
